statement.p: A spherical shell centered at the origin has an inner radius of 3 cm and an outer radius of 6 cm. The density, \delta, of the material increases linearly with the distance from the center. At the inner surface, \delta=9 g/cm{}^3; at the outer surface, \delta=18 g/cm^3.

(b) Write an integral in spherical coordinates giving the mass of the shell (for this representation, do not reduce the domain of the integral by using symmetry; type phi and theta for \phi and \theta).
(c) Find the mass of the shell.

static.solution:
(a) We use spherical coordinates. Since \delta=9 where \rho=3 and \delta=18 where \rho =6, the density increases at a rate of 3 g/cm^3 for each cm increase in radius. Thus, since density is a linear function of radius, the slope of the linear function is 3. Its equation is \delta =9 + 3(\rho - 3).
(b) Thus, \mbox{Mass } = \int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{\pi}\int_{3}^{6}(0 + 3\rho)\rho^2\sin\phi \,d\rho\,d\phi\,d\theta.
(c) Evaluating the integral, we have \mbox{Mass } = 2\pi\left(-\cos\phi\bigg|_0^{\pi}\right) \left(\left.\frac{3\rho^4}4-\frac{3\rho^3}3\right|_{3}^{6}\right) \approx 11451.1\ {\rm g}.
